page: Microsoft Azure E32bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive workloads. The instance does not include local NVMe or ephemeral SSD storage, directing all disk I/O to attached Azure Premium Storage and remote block storage services. Hardware accelerators are not present, with zero physical or virtual GPUs provisioned.

Synthetic benchmarks position the E32bs_v5 consistently within the middle 50% across general compute and memory throughput metrics. In memory bandwidth evaluations, the system recorded 140.86 GB/s on uncached 256 MB reads and 65.94 GB/s on writes, with Redis performance achieving 31.29 million SET operations per second. Multi-threaded decompression reached 85.02 GB/s in bzip3 tests, while PassMark database operations scored 15,307.83. In specialized compute tasks, Geekbench image processing placed in the top 25%, while small-model LLM text generation achieved 276.42 tokens per second. Conversely, prompt processing throughput degraded sharply on 70B parameter models, placing in the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

Given its high memory footprint, dedicated core allocation, and absence of local disks, the E32bs_v5 serves relational database management systems, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise resource planning deployments, and large-scale data transformation pipelines relying on attached high-throughput network block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E32bs_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 VNNI vector instructions. The system offers 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It contains no onboard local storage, depending entirely on remote block storage solutions like Azure Premium Storage, and omits hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show balanced performance across CPU compute and memory throughput, alongside strong scores in image processing and small-scale language model token generation. The lack of local storage requires architecting for networked disk I/O, making this instance best matched for large in-memory databases, caching layers, analytics engines, and enterprise backend applications.
